informal_statement: The modal logic KD45 is strictly weaker than S5, meaning that there are properties and theorems that can be expressed and proven in S5 that cannot be expressed or proven in KD45.
informal_proof:
First, we establish that KD45 is at least as expressive as S4, demonstrating inductively that any theorem in S4 can be proven in KD45. 

Next, we prove that KD45 is strictly weaker than S5. This is shown by constructing a specific model where S5 can prove certain axioms that KD45 cannot. 

We begin by considering the frame for S5, which is Euclidean (meaning that if world \( w \) relates to world \( u \) and \( v \), then \( u \) relates to \( v \)). Let \( \F = (\{0, 1\}, R) \) be a frame where \( a R b \) if and only if \( b = 1 \). This frame is not transitive, as \( 0 R 1 \) but \( 0 R 0 \) and \( 1 R 1 \). 

We further define the valuation \( V \) such that:
\[
V(w, p) = 
  \begin{cases}
    \{w\}, & \text{if } w = 0 \\
    \emptyset, & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}
\]
for each propositional variable \( p \). 

In this model, \( \F, V \models \Box \Box \bot \rightarrow \Box \bot \) holds because \( K(\F, V), V(0) \) is true since \( 0 \) does not satisfy \( \bot \). However, \( \F, V \not\models \Box \bot \rightarrow \Box \Box \bot \) because \( K(\F, V), V(1) \) is false due to the lack of \( \bot \).

Thus, KD45 cannot prove the equivalency that S5 enjoys, thereby demonstrating that KD45 is indeed strictly weaker than S5.

informal_statement: The modal logic system KD45 is weaker than S5 in the sense of Hilbert system ordering. Specifically, S5 contains all the axioms of KD45 plus additional axiomatic principles, which implies that any theorem provable in S5 is also provable in KD45, but not necessarily the other way around.
informal_proof:
To establish that KD45 is weaker than S5 in the sense of Hilbert system ordering, we demonstrate that the class of S5 frames includes the class of KD45 frames. This inclusion implies that any theorem valid in all S5 frames is also valid in all KD45 frames.

Given that S5 includes the axioms of KD45 plus additional axioms, any interpretation that satisfies the S5 axioms will also satisfy the KD45 axioms. Therefore, the set of all S5-frame classes is a subset of the set of all KD45-frame classes. Consequently, if a theorem is provable in S5, it is necessarily provable in KD45, establishing that KD45 is weaker than S5.

For any S5 frame, the properties such as reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, and the Euclidean property are satisfied, which are among the characteristics of KD45 frames. This alignment in frame properties further supports the inclusion of S5's frame class within KD45's frame class, thereby confirming that KD45 is indeed weaker than S5.
